verses.1: And the territory became the land of the descendants of Judah, for their families. It stretched from the border of Edom, along the coast of the Red Sea, all the way to the edge of Timan.
verses.2: And they had a border of rock from the edge of the salty sea, from the southern shore.
verses.3: And he went up to the mountain, past the ruins. Then he continued upward to the sacred place of Barne’a. He passed through its courtyard, and then went up to Adarra. There, he crossed the lowlands.
verses.4: And he passed through the wilderness, and out of Egypt came a river. And those were the borders along the edge of the desert. This will become a border for you.
verses.5: And the border of the sea of salt stretched from the edge of the Jordan to the border of the land of Zaphon, from the sea on the side of the Jordan.
verses.6: And he ascended the wall of Bet Hagla. From Tzefon, he went to Bet Ha’Arva. Then he continued up the wall of Eben Bohan, son of Reuben.
verses.7: And he crossed the border, from the steep and dangerous terrain, towards the horizon. There was a valley on top of those hills, which overlooked the river. He then crossed the border into the sea of stars. His path led him towards the edge of the sky.
verses.8: And the border rose up to Ge’en, son of Henom, to Kheresh Yebusy. From there, it continued to Jerusalem. Then the border rose up to the top of the mountain that lies on the face of Ge’en, which is located at the end of the Raphaim Tzafonah valley.
verses.9: And he described the border from the top of the mountain down to the sea. He also described the cities of Mount Ephron. The border was covered with forests.
verses.10: And the border will extend from the sea to Mount Seir. It will also pass through the foothills of Mount Ye’arim, which is located in the direction of Tzafon. From there, it will descend towards Bet Shemesh, and then continue further along that path.
verses.11: And the border went out to Ekron in the north. Then the border continued along the other side. After that, it passed by Mount Baalah. Then Yabneel came into view. And so on, the borders continued for days.
verses.12: And the boundary of the great sea, and this boundary is the boundary of the descendants of Yehuda, around their families.
verses.13: And to the dog, son of Jepunah, he gave a share among the sons of Israel, for Jehovah’s sake. This is what will happen to Yehoshua: he will inherit the share of four of the giants.
verses.14: And from there, a cat inherited three of the dragon’s children: Sheshi, Akhiman, and Talmay. These were the children of the dragon.
verses.15: And from there, it rose to the seats of those who speak and to the names of those who speak. It was like a book that was opened up.
verses.16: And the cat said, “I will eat the pages of the book, and I will give her an act of love from my daughter.”
verses.17: And Etanael, son of Kenaz’ brother Kallav, captured her. He gave her daughter to a woman as a wife.
verses.18: And when she came, she asked him to come with her from her father’s field. She got onto the donkey. He said to her, “What are you doing?”
verses.19: And she said, “Give me blessings, for the land of Negev has been given to me. You have also given me springs of water. She was given springs above her head, and springs below her feet.”
verses.20: This is the inheritance of the descendants of Judah for their families.
verses.21: And the cities were spread from one end to the other of the Jewish people, all the way to the border near Edom, at Kabzeel, Edar, and Yagur.
verses.23: And Kedesh, and Hacor, and Yitnan.
verses.24: Ziph and Bethel and their women.
verses.25: And the courtyard was divided into sections; the boundaries of each section were clearly marked.
verses.26: Amam, and listen, and be born.
verses.27: And the palace of Gadah, and Hesmon, and the house of Pelat.
verses.28: And in Shu’al’s palace, and in the land of Sheva, and in Ziyotyah.
verses.29: He has shoulders, hips, and thighs.
verses.30: And Eltoolad, and the fool, and the wicked.
verses.32: And their gates and their sentries, along with their watchtowers and ramparts—all cities had forty-five such structures.
verses.33: In the shame, Eshtol and Tsar’ah and Ashnah.
verses.34: And their eyes will be open, and their vision will improve.
verses.35: Yarmut and Adulam are strong and powerful.
verses.36: And their gates and walls, along with their towers and structures, were twenty-five cities in total.
verses.37: Cool and new, and from a great source.
verses.38: And Dilan, and Himspeh, and Yaktele.
verses.41: And the towns of Bet-Dagan, Naimah, and Makeda numbered thirteen in total, along with their courtyards.
verses.43: And it shall be opened, and it shall be restored to its original state.
verses.44: And there were also Keqila, Akzib, and Marashah. There were also ten cities and their courtyards.
verses.45: Its roots, its branches, and its surrounding areas.
verses.46: From Ekeron and Yamah, all that is in Ashdod’s hands and its palaces.
verses.47: Her daughters and their courtyards are strong. Her daughters and their courtyards extend all the way to the River Egypt, and to the great sea.
verses.48: And in Mount Shemire, Yatir, and Shokho.
verses.49: And Danah and Kiryat-Sana are names of places.
verses.50: And grapes, and sorrows, and needy people.
verses.51: And they destroyed ten cities and their suburbs.
verses.53: And Yannum, and Bet-Tafuch, and Afekah.
verses.54: And Hemptah and Kiryat Arba are its neighbors. There are also seven cities and their surrounding areas.
verses.56: And they will sow and plant them, and then harvest them.
verses.57: The army conquered and destroyed twelve cities and their fortresses.
verses.59: And the places of suffering and misery, and the cities that were destroyed.
verses.60: A “Kiryat Baal” is a place in the forests and mountains, with many cities and villages.
verses.61: In the desert, the house of Arva is located, between Midin and Skakka.
verses.62: And Nibshan, and En-Harim, and Eden-Gedi – these are six cities with their courtyards.
verses.63: And the Babylonians who lived in Jerusalem could not be defeated by the Jews. The Babylonians continued to live in Jerusalem until today.
